name: Jack Ma

controls.name: Alibaba Group
controls.role: Co-founder; left board Oct 2020; reported largest shareholder again in early 2024 (per Wikipedia)

controls.name: Ant Group (private) — economic interest via Hangzhou Junhan (~32% of Ant) alongside other employees; Junao ~22%; Alibaba 33%
controls.role: Founder; no longer controls Ant: after Dec 2023 changes to Junhan/Junao voting structures, each is controlled by a separate GP not controlled by any single person, and no shareholder controls Ant
controls.stake: Junhan ~32%, Junao ~22% of Ant (Ma's personal share not disclosed; Ma has confirmed to Alibaba his economic interest will be cut over time to no more than 8.8%)

stakes.name: Alibaba Group Holding — co-founder, retired from the company in 2020; not listed among ≥5% holders or directors in the FY2026 20-F ownership table (as of 2026-05-18; 18.67B shares outstanding), so his current stake is below 5% and undisclosed

vehicles.name: Yunfeng Funds (Yunfeng Capital)
vehicles.notes: Per Alibaba's 20-F, Ma holds minority interests in the GPs and some investment-advisor entities of several Yunfeng funds set up before his 2020 retirement, and his family holds LP interests. His GP/adviser interests are non-voting or he has waived voting, and he agreed to donate certain economic benefits to the Alibaba Group Charitable Fund or other charities. Alibaba co-invests alongside the funds

trophies.what: Bordeaux vineyards: Château de Sours, Château Guerry (Côtes de Bourg), Château Perenne (Blaye) (as of 2016, older)

policy.what: PBOC fined Ant Group 7.12B yuan (~$985M) in July 2023 for governance, consumer-protection and AML violations, ending the regulatory overhaul that began when Ant's Nov 2020 IPO was halted (older)

Pentagon added Alibaba (with Baidu and BYD) to its Section 1260H 'Chinese military companies' list in June 2026; the DoD may not contract directly with listed firms and third-party procurement bans follow from June 2027
Alibaba sued the Defense Department on 2026-06-23 seeking removal from the 1260H list, calling the designation 'arbitrary and capricious'

giving.name: Jack Ma Foundation (est. Sept 2018; education, environment, public health)

watch.what: Alibaba v. Department of Defense (1260H designation) — court ruling; Xiaomi and AMEC previously won removal through litigation
Ant Group IPO revival or further Junhan/Junao restructuring (Alibaba holds a right of first refusal on transfers until a qualified Ant IPO)

gaps: Pass 2 swaps the Wikipedia-sourced 1260H items, Ant control, and the Ant fine for CNBC, Japan Times and Alibaba's FY2026 20-F; those Wikipedia URLs are retracted. The earlier Alibaba 'controls' entry (cited to Wikipedia/Jack_Ma) is superseded by the 'stakes' entry, since Ma has no board seat and holds under 5%. Still unverified: his exact Alibaba share count (not in the 20-F), Jack Ma Foundation details, the Bordeaux vineyards, and any real estate.
